description: One of the earliest proponents of abstract painting in Europe, Frantisek Kupka immigrated from Bohemia (in the present-day Czech Republic) to Paris in 1896. Traveling to Paris and Chartres, France, he studied the stained-glass windows of Gothic and Romanesque cathedrals and created radiant abstractions that convey the feeling of light passing through colored glass.
title: Reminiscence of a Cathedral
